An oil firm, Barama Energy Resources, in partnership with the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, has inaugurated a Compressed Natural Gas station at the Defence Headquarters in Abuja, marking the beginning of plans to establish similar facilities across military formations nationwide. The facility, inaugurated on Friday at Mogadishu Cantonment, is designed to provide cheaper and cleaner fuel for military personnel and members of the public, while supporting the Federal Government’s drive to promote alternative energy sources. Speaking at the ceremony, the Chief Executive Officer of Barama Energy Partners, Dipo Jimoh, described the project as a demonstration of the benefits of strategic partnerships, expressing the company’s readiness to collaborate with NNPC Limited on similar projects across the country. “This is progress through partnership. Our plan is to work with NNPC to execute more projects across Nigeria,” Jimoh said. He added that the facility was completed within a short period and that its safety installations and operational standards reflect the company’s commitment to quality service delivery. “We’ve been able to demonstrate this by the execution of this first one. We did this within a short period of time, and, as you can see, it was done seamlessly, well executed. The safety apparatus is 100 per cent. “You have to give the best to the military. This will be a 24-hour service station,” he said. He also commended the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority for granting the necessary approvals for the project. He noted that the collaboration brings together two critical components of national development: energy security and national security. “At NNPC, we firmly recognise that energy security is an integral component of our national security,” Ahmed said. He explained that the facility has a capacity of 1,500 standard cubic metres of gas and can serve 100 vehicles at full capacity. He added that the partnership will be extended to other military locations through the development of strategic energy hubs and additional CNG facilities. “It is the first of several strategic initiatives we are working on with the Defence Headquarters, and our ambition is to replicate this partnership across strategic military locations nationwide,” he said. Ahmed further disclosed that NNPCL is at an advanced stage of discussions with the Defence Headquarters on a proposed modern filling station and integrated energy hub in Maitama, Abuja. According to him, the proposed facility will provide integrated energy solutions and help reduce energy costs by up to 60 per cent through the transition from conventional liquid fuels to CNG. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas, Ismail Ahmed, commended the military for embracing the Federal Government’s alternative fuel programme. He said the initiative is working with the Armed Forces to establish energy hubs in military barracks with significant population densities. Ahmed disclosed that about 150 military personnel have undergone a train-the-trainer programme on CNG, adding that the initiative is awaiting their graduation. He noted that the transition to alternative fuels will help reduce the military’s operational expenditure, particularly the cost of transportation. In his remarks, the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede—represented by the Chief of Defence Logistics, Maj. Gen. Wisdom Etuk—said the inauguration aligns with the military’s efforts to diversify its energy sources and reduce dependence on conventional fuels. He disclosed that the Defence Headquarters plans to acquire four CNG daughter stations as the first phase of the initiative.
